extracted.intended_audience: writers, workshop participants, MFA students, choreographers and arts educators who give/receive critique
extracted.subtask_description: Applying Liz Lerman's Critical Response Process (CRP) as a structured workshop method for giving and receiving creative-works feedback, where the artist controls the agenda and responders follow specific question/response rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements of Meaning (Step 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responders share what was 'meaningful, evocative, interesting, exciting, and/or striking' in the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be specific and observation-based; banned: vague praise such as 'it was good' or 'I liked it.' Focus on concrete moments or elements that produced impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist as Questioner (Step 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The maker asks the responders questions about the work; the maker controls what aspects of the work get critiqued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shifts power away from responders' agendas and lets the artist direct attention to areas where they want feedback. The artist decides which questions to pose and which critiques to invite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutral Questions (Step 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responders ask questions about the work that are neutral—i.e., not opinions masked as questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed example: 'What was your intention with the last paragraph?' Banned example: 'Why did the last paragraph end so abruptly?' (this is an opinion disguised as a question). Frame questions to elicit information rather than make evaluative claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissioned Opinions (Step 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responders may offer opinions only if the artist gives permission to hear them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responders should ask for permission before offering evaluative comments (e.g., 'I have an opinion about the ending — do you want to hear it?'). The artist may accept or decline; permission controls when quality judgments are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific moments of impact as legitimate critique
rubrics_metrics.description: The workshop privileges identification and discussion of specific moments of meaning or impact in the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique should point to discrete instances that affected responders (scenes, lines, images) rather than generalities; tie observations to the text/performances to be useful to the maker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on artist's intentions and unanswered questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The artist's intentions and any questions they pose are central, and addressing those intentions/unanswered questions is a valid focus of critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responders should use the artist's questions to guide feedback; critique should help reveal whether the work communicates the artist's intent or leaves productive ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutral inquiry into structural and craft choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions should probe structure and craft choices in a neutral way that helps the artist see how choices are functioning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask exploratory, nonjudgmental questions about pacing, structure, voice, transitions, and other craft elements so the artist can decide whether to act on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissioned opinion on quality as a late-stage dimension
rubrics_metrics.description: Opinions about quality are allowed but only after the artist has signaled openness to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves the workshop's focus on discovery before judgment; when invited, opinions should be offered thoughtfully and with specific references to the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist ownership of the critique conversation (underlying assumption)
rubrics_metrics.description: The artist owns both the work and the conversation about it; feedback is organized around the artist's needs and choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responders defer to the artist's agency in deciding what to hear and act upon; the process is designed to support the artist's momentum and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback should leave the maker eager and motivated
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback's purpose is to help the maker feel eager and motivated to get back to work rather than demoralized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame responses so they enable forward movement; avoid destructive or vague comments that sap motivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique as creative, not merely diagnostic
rubrics_metrics.description: The process treats critique as part of the creative work—constructive, generative, and exploratory—not just a checklist of problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage observations and questions that open possibilities and support the artist's creative decisions rather than only listing faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague praise (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vague positive comments (e.g., 'it was good' / 'I liked it') are harmful because they provide no actionable information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace vague praise with specific statements of effect (what was striking, why it worked for you) so the artist gains usable insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifiable moments of meaning/impact (short-fiction implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: For short fiction, responders should identify clear moments that produced meaning or impact for readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to sentences, images, lines of dialogue, or scenes and describe their effect on you as a reader; this helps the writer understand what is resonating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence between artist intention and reader experience (short-fiction implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the reader's experience aligns with the artist's stated or discernible intentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use neutral questions and statements of meaning to reveal mismatches or alignment between intent and reception, enabling the writer to adjust clarity or ambiguity intentionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft choices must be visible enough to be neutrally questioned (short-fiction implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers should make craft choices (voice, structure, pacing, point of view) legible so responders can ask neutral, informative questions about them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a choice is opaque, responders should ask neutral questions to surface it rather than make assumptions or offer premature judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work's invitation to dialogue vs. closure (short-fiction implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the story invites further dialogue/questions or aims for closure; both are artistic choices worth neutral examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responders can neutrally probe whether the degree of openness or closure serves the story's intent and the reader's experience.
